Dhaka diplomatic zone on high alert after email threats
item.description:
Security has been tightened across Dhaka’s diplomatic zone following email threats sent to several foreign embassies, with missions in Gulshan and Baridhara placed under heightened surveillance.
Additional law enforcement personnel in uniform and plain clothes have been deployed, while checkpoints, patrols and surveillance around the embassies have been increased. Quick Response Teams have also been kept on standby.
Additional Deputy Commissioner Abu Khayer of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police’s (DMP) Diplomatic Security Division told Dhaka Tribune that police had not received any written complaint over the threats.
“The Chinese embassy informed Police Headquarters of the matter through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The Counter Terrorism and Transnational Crime (CTTC) unit is investigating the incident,” he said.
Abu Khayer said there was no reason to panic, as adequate security measures had been put in place across the diplomatic zone.
“We do not know who issued the threats, why they were issued or which embassies received them, as we have not been informed in writing,” he said, adding that police had heightened security after learning of the incident.
Meanwhile, representatives of several foreign missions held a meeting with CTTC officials over the threats, and the counter-terrorism unit has launched an investigation.
Sources said several foreign embassies in Dhaka received threatening emails late last week, which police suspect were intended to spread panic. Police also said no general diary (GD) or written complaint had been filed with Gulshan Police Station over the threats.

item.title: PM asks giving priority to merit in promotion of forces
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Sunday asked the members of the Navy and Air Force Selection Board to give priority to merit, competence, leadership qualities, discipline, integrity, loyalty and suitability for the promotion of officers without being influenced by political ideology or personal preference.
“Bangladesh Navy and Air Force, alongside safeguarding the country’s independence and sovereignty, have been making crucial contributions to maintaining internal peace, discipline and stability and assisting the civil administration in tackling disasters,” he said.
The prime minister said this while inaugurating the Navy and Air Force Selection Board-2026 at the Air Force Headquarters this morning, said his Deputy Press Secretary Jahidul Islam Rony.
The board will consider eligible officers of the Bangladesh Navy holding the ranks of captain, commander and lieutenant commander and officers of the Bangladesh Air Force holding the ranks of group captain, wing commander and squadron leader for promotion to the next ranks.
On his arrival at the Air Force Headquarters, the prime minister was received by his Defence Adviser Brigadier General (retd) Dr AKM Shamsul Islam, Chief of Army Staff General Waker-Uz-Zaman, Chief of Naval Staff Admiral Khondkar Misbah ul Azim and Chief of Air Staff Air Chief Marshal Hasan Mahmood Khan.
Before opening the selection board, the prime minister adorned Chief of Naval Staff Khandker Misbah Ul Azim with the Admiral rank badge and congratulated him on his appointment as the new Navy chief.
Admiral Khandker Misbah ul Azim expressed gratitude to the prime minister on behalf of the Bangladesh Navy and sought his guidance to further develop the force as a modern, capable and time-befitting navy.
In his address to the selection board, the prime minister paid tribute to Shaheed President Ziaur Rahman and former Prime Minister Begum Khaleda Zia.
He also recalled with deep respect the martyrs of the 1971 Liberation War, the martyrs of the 2024 mass uprising, and those who were killed or injured in movements for democracy and people’s rights from 1971 to 2024.
He paid homage to all martyrs, wounded freedom fighters and valiant freedom fighters of the Liberation War, particularly the martyrs and heroes of the armed forces, including the Navy and Air Force.
The prime minister thanked the chiefs and all members of the Navy and Air Force for their sacrifice and contribution to the country.
He later inspected several important operational installations of the Bangladesh Air Force.
At the Air Defence Operations Centre (ADOC) in Dhaka Cantonment, he unveiled the inaugural plaque of the Air Defence System Integration (ADSI) and inspected its air defence activities.
He also visited the Air Command Operations Centre (ACOC), where he observed through its Digital Large Display the interception of enemy aircraft by Air Force fighter aircraft and troops insertion by helicopters using a live feed from unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) operating from Chittagong.
Later, the prime minister visited the Aerospace Research and Development Complex (ARDC) and observed its research activities.
During the visit, different types of indigenous UAVs developed by the Bangladesh Air Force, including drones, kamikaze drones, interceptor drones and vertical take-off and landing (VTOL) UAVs, were displayed. He also observed the flight of a quadcopter.
The prime minister expressed hope that developing such advanced aerial systems through the Air Force’s own technological capabilities would mark significant progress in research, innovation and technological self-reliance.
The defence adviser to the prime minister, chiefs of the Navy and Air Force, principal staff officer of the Armed Forces Division, defence secretary and senior officials of the armed forces were present.

Salma Adil foundation extends support to flood-affected students in Banshkhali
item.description:
Salma Adil Foundation has extended a helping hand to students affected by the recent devastating floods in Banshkhali, Chattogram, by distributing essential educational materials among them.

On the afternoon of 22 August, educational materials were distributed at two government primary schools in Banshkhali through an initiative funded by the Salma Adil Foundation and organised by Banshkhali Times.

At West Chechuria Ghonapara Government Primary School and Baraitali Government Primary School, new school bags and guidebooks were handed over to students whose education had been disrupted by the floods.

The programme was conducted by Lecturer Jahedul Islam Tuku. Among those present were Abu Obaida Arafat, editor of Banshkhali Times; poet Arkanul Islam; Salma Adil Foundation representatives Imtiaz Uddin and Akibul Haque; Mizan Bin Taher, member Secretary of Banshkhali Press Club; Asim Kumar Dey, head teacher of West Chechuria Ghonapara Government Primary School; and Md Ashek Urahman Chowdhury, head Teacher of Baraitali Government Primary School.

Speaking at the programme, the guests expressed their appreciation to Lion Salma Adil, founder of the Salma Adil Foundation, for her continued commitment to humanitarian causes. They noted that the foundation has been supporting underprivileged and vulnerable communities through various initiatives for a long time.

Since the recent floods hit Banshkhali, the foundation has also undertaken relief efforts on a significant scale, earning appreciation from the local community.

The speakers further highlighted that providing educational materials to flood-affected students is a meaningful initiative that can help them return to their studies and continue their education despite the challenges caused by the disaster.

The students received the new school bags and guidebooks with visible excitement and happiness. Their cheerful smiles reflected the joy and encouragement brought by this thoughtful gesture.

item.title: Criminal gang would collect specialists' details for extortion: DB
item.description:
The Detective Branch (DB) of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) has arrested four people for allegedly collecting personal information about specialist physicians and demanding money from them.

DMP Additional Commissioner and DB chief Shafiqul Islam disclosed the information at a press conference on Sunday at the DMP headquarters on Minto Road in Dhaka.

At the press conference, Shafiqul Islam said a gang had targeted at least five specialist physicians at government and private hospitals. They included Professor Md Asadur Rahman of the Department of Ear, Nose and Throat and Head-Neck Surgery at Dhaka Medical College Hospital, and Professor AKM Aminul Haque of the Department of Internal Medicine at Anwar Khan Modern Hospital.

The gang demanded extortion money from the physicians in US dollars. Asadur Rahman was attacked after refusing to pay. Four of the seven gang members have been arrested.

According to the DB, the gang collected information about doctors’ home and chamber addresses and their children through food-delivery apps. They then identified financially well-off doctors and demanded extortion money in dollars over the phone.

On 27 July, five men stopped doctor Aminul Haque’s car on Dhanmondi Road 4 and threatened him. On the night of 17 August, doctor Asadur Rahman was attacked in Shantinagar. People at the scene informed the police, who later detained a man named Jibon alias Adil. The others fled.

Asadur Rahman subsequently filed a case with Paltan Model Police Station. According to the case statement, an unknown number had called him several days before the attack and demanded US$15,000 in extortion money.

Shafiqul Islam said the DB launched an investigation to identify those involved in the attack. As part of the investigation, Sani Saha, 38, was arrested in Shonir Akhra and Fatin Israq Labib, 20, in Khilkhet on Saturday night. Two others had already been arrested in the case. Four members of the gang are now in custody.

According to the DB, Sani Saha was one of the key figures behind the gang. He worked in Singapore from 2022 to 2025. He later became involved in hundi transactions and suffered losses of Tk 50 million. He subsequently became involved in extortion to recover the money, according to the DB.

The DB said Sani met Alamgir Hossain while he was in Singapore in 2023. Sani was later tasked with collecting personal information about wealthy people, including their home addresses, vehicle registration numbers, professions, movements and financial circumstances. He was also assigned to extort large sums of money from doctors Aminul Haque and Asadur Rahman.

Sani later tasked Fatin with recruiting people for the attacks. During interrogation, Fatin reportedly said he recruited Abu Bakar, 18, Ratul, 19, Iban, 22, Jibon, 21, and Sabbir, 18, for Tk 100,000 to carry out the attack on Asadur Rahman. Iban and Jibon have been arrested and are in jail.

Shafiqul Islam said the gang also targeted senior government officials in addition to physicians. Another gang has been threatening various embassies by email, he said, adding that the DB is also working to identify and arrest its members.

item.title: Zonta club launches sustainable initiative for mother and child welfare
item.description:
Zonta Club of Sonargaon, in collaboration with the Begum Rokeya Women and Child Development Organization, has launched a special initiative aimed at improving the quality of life for underprivileged women and children, reports a press release.

A ceremony marking the occasion was held today, Saturday (August 22), at the Begum Rokeya Organisation’s center in Uttara.

As part of this initiative, the organisation announced the adoption of two children, the donation of a wheelchair to a child with special needs, and the rollout of training programs for women.

Additionally, an interactive counseling session was conducted for underprivileged women and children, emphasising awareness against child marriage.

Lajina Mona, president of Zonta Club of Sonargaon, said, "Zonta International is a century-old service organisation based in the USA, actively working across Nepal, Sri Lanka, India, and Bangladesh. In Bangladesh, we operate through seven clubs—six in Dhaka and one in Chattogram- supported by a dedicated youth volunteer team. Today, we came together to adopt a mother and child, while promoting the importance of hygiene and raising awareness about the harms of child marriage. Moving forward, we aim to provide accessible medical support and expand our projects beyond Dhaka."

Highlighting the role of youth leadership, Ayaan Manzur Rahman, youth president of Zonta Club of Sonargaon, added, "I joined volunteer work back in the eighth grade. I strongly encourage young people to engage in community service because Gen Z represents the future of our nation. It is inspiring to see young volunteers participating with such genuine enthusiasm."

The outreach program was conducted with the support of the Begum Rokeya Women and Child Development Organization.

Operating since 1997, the organisation provides healthcare services for mothers and children, speech therapy for children with special needs, food and care for the elderly, maternal healthcare, child vaccinations, educational scholarships, and affordable medicines.

item.title: Bangladesh signed up for AI-enabled healthcare, what should that actually mean?
item.description:
In December 2025, in a conference room in Tokyo, Bangladesh signed a document that researchers in my field had been waiting years to see. The National Health Compact, agreed at the UHC High-Level Forum, lists six pillars for reforming the country's health system by 2030 (National Health Compact, Bangladesh, UHC High-Level Forum, Tokyo, December 2025).

Tucked into the sixth one is a line that most readers probably skimmed past: the government commits to supporting "the scale-up of digital health solutions, AI-enabled tools, and other emerging technologies that enhance equitable, efficient, and high-quality service delivery."

I read that sentence more than once. It's the first time I've seen AI named directly in a Bangladeshi health policy document rather than treated as something for another country to figure out first. But a compact is not a blueprint. It says AI-enabled tools should scale up. It doesn't say which tools, for which pillar, solving which specific problem. That gap is where my own work sits, and I think it's worth spelling out what filling that gap could actually involve.

Why the gap matters more here than elsewhere

Bangladesh's public health spending was 0.40 per cent of GDP as of 2021, well behind Bhutan at 2.21 per cent, Nepal at 1.80 per cent, and even Pakistan at 0.84 per cent. Out-of-pocket costs make up 73 per cent of total health spending, one of the highest shares in South Asia, and that burden has been pushing people into poverty. Health costs pushed 3.74 per cent of the population below the 2.15 dollar a day poverty line in 2016, up from 3.11 per cent in 2010. The health budget for FY2024-25 came to just 0.74 per cent of GDP (Centre for Policy Dialogue, Policy Brief 2025(2), April 2025).

In a system this constrained, a badly targeted tool doesn't just underperform. It actively wastes money the country doesn't have to waste. That's the argument for getting the "how" right before scaling anything up.

Where the compact's pillars point

The compact's second pillar calls for expanding community-based and telehealth service delivery, especially in hard-to-reach areas. I built a chatbot for dengue symptom triage in Bangladesh, designed to run on simple decision-tree logic in low-bandwidth clinical settings in Bengali and English. In testing on 2019-2023 case data, the model correctly flagged severe cases well enough to be useful as a first filter, and in a small pilot with 50 users, three in four said they were satisfied with it. It''s a small example, but it points at something the compact gestures toward without detailing: triage tools that work where the internet is slow and the nearest doctor is an hour away, not just in Dhaka.

The third pillar talks about redesigning the Essential Service Package around life-course prevention, including maternal health. My colleagues and I built a tool for maternal health risk prediction that combines two approaches: a set of medical rules a doctor would recognise, and a machine-learning model trained on patient data. We tested it against clinical data and then asked actual doctors, 14 of them, to review its recommendations. When we showed them the combined version, the one that explains its reasoning in terms they recognize rather than just a risk score, more than half said they would trust it enough to use in practice. That distinction between a tool that shows its work and one that doesn't seems small on paper. To a doctor deciding whether to refer a patient, it isn't.

The fifth pillar is where things get more complicated, and more interesting. It commits to establishing a National Health Security Office to manage a National Health Fund and lead what it calls strategic purchasing, while targeting vulnerable groups, urban slum residents, widows, people over 70, people with disabilities, for prioritized services.

This is not a new idea in Bangladesh. A draft National Health Protection Act has existed since 2014, proposing something similar: a National Health Protection Authority, a health card system, and lists sorting citizens into income categories, below poverty, marginal income, middle income, and above, to determine who gets subsidized care (Draft National Health Protection Act, 2014). The draft law even requires annual audits and treats misuse of the system as a punishable offense. More than a decade later, the compact is effectively picking up where that draft left off, this time with an actual signed commitment and a 2030 deadline attached.

Here's the part I keep coming back to. Any list sorting citizens into income categories is a judgment call, whether or not anyone calls it that. Someone, or something, decides who counts as "below poverty level" versus "marginal income," and that decision determines who gets a subsidized health card and who doesn't. If this system gets digitized without checking for bias first, and I've seen this exact pattern before in disaster aid allocation, it risks locking in existing unfairness at a much larger scale and a much faster pace than a paper-based system ever could. The bias-correction techniques I used to fix historical unfairness in post-flood aid rankings, adjusting a model so it stops treating location as a shortcut for actual need, apply directly to this kind of eligibility list too.

I want to be careful here about a second idea some of my recent work touches on: using AI to flag suspicious claims once a national health fund is up and running. That's a real and useful application in principle. But I''ll say plainly that my own research on this, which mixes rule-based logic with pattern recognition, has so far been tested only on simulated financial data built for a research paper, not on real claims from any health system, and my own paper is explicit that those results shouldn't be read as proof the method works on real-world fraud. It's a promising direction. It is not a finished tool, and Bangladesh shouldn't wait for it to be one before doing the more basic work of auditing its eligibility data for bias.

Bangladeshi researchers have working models for triage, maternal risk prediction, and privacy-preserving collaboration across institutions, at different stages of readiness. None of this needs to be imported or reinvented from scratch

The piece nobody wants to think about until it breaks

The compact's first and sixth pillars also call for modernizing infrastructure and expanding private sector participation, including private diagnostic centers. Bangladesh's health data will increasingly sit across public hospitals, NGO clinics, and private providers that have no particular incentive to share patient records with each other, and plenty of legal and ethical reasons not to.

This is the kind of problem a technique called federated learning is built for, where separate institutions train a shared model together without any of them handing over their raw patient data. I built a framework called MedHE to test exactly this idea, combining that data-sharing approach with encryption strong enough that even the central server coordinating the process can't read what any single institution contributed. In our tests, simulating five separate clients working together on a health-related text classification task, the encrypted, privacy-protected version performed statistically as well as an ordinary shared model, while cutting the amount of data that needed to move between institutions by more than 97 per cent.

It's still a research demonstration rather than something running across real Bangladeshi hospitals, but it shows the privacy problem and the efficiency problem can be solved together, not traded off against each other. Bangladesh's own Digital Health Strategy, in place since 2023, will need something in this direction eventually if it's serious about connecting a fragmented network of providers without asking any of them to give up their patients' privacy first.

What would actually make this real

The compact already has a monitoring framework with real targets: raising the UHC service coverage index from 54 to 65 by 2030, cutting the share of households facing catastrophic health spending from 42 per cent to 35 per cent, and more (National Health Compact, Bangladesh, 2025). A few additions would make the AI-enabled tools commitment more than a sentence in a document.

First, any tool used to determine eligibility or priority for the National Health Fund should be checked for bias before it goes live, the same way financial and clinical outcomes are already tracked.

Second, fairness and explainability deserve their own line in the compact''s list of indicators, not just a mention under one pillar. What gets measured tends to be what gets built.

Third, the government should draw on the research already happening inside the country. Bangladeshi researchers have working models for triage, maternal risk prediction, and privacy-preserving collaboration across institutions, at different stages of readiness. None of this needs to be imported or reinvented from scratch.

Fourth, the long-dormant National Health Protection Act should be revisited with this compact in mind. A legal framework for a health card system already exists in draft form. Updating it with explicit rules for checking algorithms for bias would save the country from relearning lessons other systems have already paid for.

I think about the years between that 2014 draft act and this 2025 compact, and how much could have been built in between if the tools had been treated as ready rather than hypothetical. Some of them are ready now. Others still need more testing before anyone should trust them with real decisions, and it matters to be honest about which is which. Bangladesh has already signed the intention. What remains is turning one sentence in a Tokyo hotel conference room into something that actually makes a difference to a patient in Sunamganj or Satkhira.

item.description:
Police in Latur district of Maharashtra, India have registered a case against Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) convener Abhijeet Dipke and others for allegedly entering a government school without permission, disrupting official work and threatening teachers.
The FIR was registered at Ausa police station following a complaint by Sayyed Shamshadbano Khairatali, 53, a teacher at a Zilla Parishad Urdu school. Dipke has been visiting government schools across the district and highlighting their problems as part of the CJP’s ongoing “School Thik Karo” (Improve Government Schools) campaign.
According to the complaint, the incident took place at the ZP Urdu school in Jawali near Ausa, more than 500km from Mumbai.
Dipke and his associates allegedly entered the school without permission, sat among the students and questioned them, disrupting educational and official activities, reports The Hindu.
The complaint also alleged that Dipke filmed the proceedings and shared the footage on social media.
It further alleged that he defamed the school by claiming that students from another school had been brought in and made to sit in classrooms during his visit, and threatened to get the teachers suspended.
The case was registered under Sections 132 (assault or use of criminal force to deter a public servant from performing official duties), 329(3) (house trespass), 351(2) (criminal intimidation) and 356(2) (criminal defamation) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.
Further investigation is underway, officials said.

The question the Mecca pact has raised for Bangladesh
item.description:
To Muslims, Mecca is much more than any city. It is significant that the rulers of Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan chose this city as the place to sign a defence pact. Even selecting Friday for the pact signing holds similar importance.

This trilateral alliance may desire a religious facade, something that Mohammed bin Salman, Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, and Shehbaz Sharif may have been hoping for. Such a religious facade might help them in terms of voter polarisation in their respective countries. While these rulers have done little to significantly curb the aggressors in Gaza.

Signing any agreement in Mecca on a Friday also shows the firmness of their commitment. Questions arise as to what exactly these countries seek to protect with this defence agreement? Does the convergence of these three mid-sized military powers bear additional significance for South Asia?

Strategic diversification begins on all fronts

These trilateral signatories do not share borders. Thus, it cannot be called a regional alliance. It can be assumed that Saudi Arabia's extra interest is what has drawn Shehbaz Sharif and Erdoğan to Mecca.

The rulers in the Middle East who have long relied on the United States to protect their thrones are gradually seeing that longstanding advantage come to an end. The royal families of this region have been safely ensconced in such a security arrangement for a long time. However, by challenging the US -Israel axis, Iran has shattered the old sense of security for Washington's Arab allies.

Many countries around the world have taken immediate lessons from this scenario. Everyone is reevaluating and rearranging their defence policies and strategies. Strategic diversification has started everywhere.

The Mecca Agreement is its first major manifestation. The harsh reality has brought these three distant powers closer. Moreover, without relinquishing decision-making freedom, all those involved in the agreement were able to add additional weight to their international image. Yet, Riyadh-Washington and Islamabad-Beijing ties persist. Turkey does not have to leave NATO either.

The economic backdrop of this agreement is also worth considering. Gulf countries serve as major centres for global capitalism. Iran's counterattack in the face of aggression has shaken down assets and investments in that area. Securing these capitalist centres is crucial for many. Hence, the Mecca Agreement does not solely involve the interests of three countries; it has a significant political economy component. However, more than the moment of the agreement, everyone is interested in seeing how much importance the three countries attach to utilising it. It's still unclear whether it will have a unitary command structure like NATO.

The Mecca agreement brings India and Israel closer

The conflict between Iran and Israel and the US and its consequences have set the backdrop for this agreement. All three signing rulers are more or less close to the US. For these reasons, many have wondered whether Iran was the intended counterpart to the agreement. Some may also have thought of Israel.

News emerged that just before the agreement was signed, the Prime Minister of Israel called the Prime Minister of India. Naturally, the question arises, how significant is this agreement for them? Particularly against the backdrop of India's adversarial relationship with Pakistan, has this trilateral military alliance created additional pressure for New Delhi? Will they, therefore, seek to join with someone else to enhance their ''defense'' capability.

The agreement states that if any of the three allies are attacked, it will be considered an attack on all three countries. This clause is similar to NATO's Article 5. This also means that in any future India-Pakistan war, Turkey and Saudi Arabia will stand by Islamabad. Or, in any Iran-Saudi military conflict, Pakistan and Turkey will fight against Tehran. Pakistan has already deployed some air defence systems and troops in Saudi Arabia. Prior to this trilateral agreement, Pakistan had signed another separate military agreement with Saudi Arabia in the previous September. The subsequent agreement is undoubtedly a significant advancement over the previous one.

These are clear indications that military thinking and structure are set for upheaval in Asia. Pakistan’s Deputy Prime Minister has already said, "This agreement is open to other countries as well." After his statement, curiosity has arisen about which other countries might be potential partners.

The call from Netanyahu to Narendra Modi ahead of the Mecca Agreement signing is certainly indicative. Saudi Arabia, Turkey, or Pakistan is not currently facing any new hostilities. But they have taken the news of this military alliance of three Muslim-majority countries as a distant warning signal. This is equally true for Iran.

Turkey has competition with Tel Aviv in Syria and other places. Besides Iran, several Israeli politicians have recently labeled Turkey as a ''threat'' despite Turkey being their oldest diplomatic friend in the Muslim world. They also find the nuclear capability of Muslim-majority Pakistan to be ‘dangerous’. For these reasons, Tel Aviv has no reason to view this trilateral agreement favourably. On 9 August, the Jerusalem Post wrote, "The Mecca Agreement will further develop Israel-India relations." Both countries want to bring the UAE closer to the same goal.

Under pressure of increased militarisation in South Asia

The Mecca Agreement has also posed new questions for Bangladesh. Should Bangladesh become part of such a coalition? Or, in response to increased Israel-India military proximity, what should be Bangladesh's course of action? Surely, policy makers in Bangladesh have already begun to ponder these questions.

The way the US-Iran conflict is coming to an end has helped create a strong and courageous image of Tehran in the Muslim world. To maintain leadership positions in Muslim-majority countries, Saudi Arabia and Turkey have entered a competition. They will continually seek Bangladesh as a partner to manage that rivalry. Turkey has shown a keen interest in enhancing military relations with Bangladesh for two to three years.

Simultaneously, the Indo-Pakistan military competition in South Asia is accelerating rapidly. Increased India-Israel closeness as a reaction to the trilateral agreement will undoubtedly intensify military rivalry in South Asia. As a side effect, we may witness numerous regional proxy wars.

Pakistan's economy was unable to sustain its vast military structure and manpower. Yet, its military personnel enriched with experiences from many wars. Saudi finance and Turkey's military industry could rejuvenate this. All three countries will benefit from this process.

In response, if advanced Israeli technology starts entering India's military framework, New Delhi's military capabilities will also reach new heights. Post-Mecca Agreement, the motivation to form a counter-military block among India's policymakers is increasing. Serious discussions about the trilateral defence agreement are underway there.

Such retaliatory agreements and coalitions will impact and pressure Bangladesh, Nepal, and Sri Lanka. These countries find it challenging to match the militarisation of larger powers. These nations have been floundering to address the economic crisis sparked by wars in the Middle East in recent months. Now ahead of them awaits a long-term militarily complex phase. Just as the Mecca Agreement directly connects Turkey and Saudi Arabia with the situation in South Asia, it has also driven Israel’s increased activism.

*Altaf Parvez is a researcher on history

item.title: Junior Scholarship Examination to begin on 8 December, 6 instructions for candidates
item.description:
The schedule for the 2026 Junior Scholarship Examination has been published. The examination will begin on 8 December. Candidates sitting the examination will have to follow six special instructions.

The Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education, Dhaka published the schedule for the Junior Scholarship Examination today, Sunday (23 August). It also issued six instructions for the candidates.

According to the schedule, the Bangla examination will be held on 8 December, English on 10 December, Mathematics on 13 December, while Science and Bangladesh and Global Studies exam will be held on 15 December.

Junior scholarship exam: How to get results

Earlier, the education calendar published by the Ministry of Education had announced the tentative schedule for the Junior Scholarship Examination and the expected date for publication of the results.

According to the calendar, the examination was scheduled to begin on 15 December and continue until 20 December. The tentative date for publication of the results was set for 30 December.

However, under the new decision, the Junior Scholarship Examination will begin and end earlier than scheduled.

6 instructions candidates must follow—

  • Candidates must take their seats in the examination hall at least 30 minutes before the examination begins.

  • The examination must be conducted according to the time specified on the question paper. The Science examination will be held for one and a half hours (1 hour 30 minutes), followed by one and a half hours (1 hour 30 minutes) for Bangladesh and Global Studies, making a total examination time of three hours (3 hours).

  • Candidates must collect their admit cards from the heads of their respective institutions at least seven days before the examination begins.

  • Candidates must correctly write and shade their roll number, registration number, subject code and other required information on the OMR form of their answer scripts. Under no circumstances may the answer script be folded.

  • Candidates may use ordinary scientific calculators approved by the education board during the examination.

  • No person other than the centre secretary, and no candidate, may bring a mobile phone or any other electronic device into the examination centre.

Class-XI admissions to begin 2 Sept, classes 23 Sept; find out all the details

Mark distribution—

This year, students will sit for examinations carrying a total of 400 marks. Based on the marks obtained, talent pool and general scholarships will be awarded. Bangla, English and Mathematics will each carry 100 marks.

Students will have three hours for each of these subjects. Science and Bangladesh and Global Studies will carry 100 marks in total, with 50 marks for each subject. The examination for these two subjects will be held for a total of three hours, with one and a half hours allocated to each subject.

item.title: Four family members killed one after another for stopping yaba use: Police
item.description:
Police have detained two young men over the killing of four members of the same family in Machhuapara of the Kamalkachhna area in Rangpur city. According to police, the two planned and carried out the killings of former Rangpur Zilla School teacher Ganapati Chakraborty, his wife and their two children after he tried to stop them from using yaba. They later scattered household belongings in an attempt to make the killings appear to be a robbery.

Police Commissioner Mohammad Abdul Mabud disclosed the information at a press conference at his office at around 1:30 pm today, Sunday. The two detainees are Siddhartha Das, 19, and Mugdha Das, 23. They are cousins. They were detained from the Dakhiganj cremation ground area of the city early this morning. Their homes are located near that of the slain Ganapati Chakraborty.

2 detained over killings of four members of a family in Rangpur

Police Commissioner Mohammad Abdul Mabud said Mugdha and Siddhartha climbed onto the roof of the second floor of Ganapati Chakraborty’s under-construction three-storey house from a neighbouring building in Machhuapara, Rangpur city, on Thursday night. They were using yaba there. Hearing noises, Ganapati Chakraborty went to the open rooftop of the second floor and tried to stop them from using the drug. At that point, the two young men killed him by strangling him with a towel.

When Ganapati Chakraborty’s wife, Pritilata Chakraborty, 50, heard his screams and tried to go to the rooftop, she was killed on the stairs. Their daughter, Agami Chakraborty, 25, was then killed when she attempted to go upstairs. Their 13-year-old son, Ayush Chakraborty, who was asleep in a room, was also strangled to death afterwards.

The police commissioner said the two detainees were already known to the victims. Fearing that their identities would be exposed, Mugdha and Siddhartha killed all four members of the family one after another.

Police recovered the bodies of Ganapati Chakraborty, 65, his wife Pritilata Chakraborty, 50, their daughter Agami Chakraborty, 25, and son Ayush Chakraborty, 13, from the first floor of the house on Saturday night. Ganapati Chakraborty lived there with his family. Construction of the ground and second floors of the building remains incomplete.

Police said Mugdha Das works at a fish shop in the city’s City Bazar, while Siddhartha Das has been working as a craftsman at a jewellery shop in Rangpur for about eight years.

The police commissioner said that after the killings, Mugdha and Siddhartha remained at the house. They bathed there, took dates and cucumbers out of the refrigerator and ate them, and used yaba. They left the house on Friday when the streets were relatively empty during Jummah prayers. Before leaving, they opened cupboards and drawers and scattered clothes and other belongings everywhere.

'Who killed my sister, brother-in-law and their children?

The press conference said that items used for taking yaba were found on a table inside the house. Evidence was also found suggesting an attempt had been made to test a gold bangle using fire. Based on these clues, Mugdha and Siddhartha were identified and detained. During questioning, police said, they confessed to the killings. Gold jewellery looted from the victims’ home has been recovered from an abandoned place indicated by the two detainees.

According to police, two mobile phones belonging to the slain family had been submerged in water mixed with detergent, possibly in an attempt to destroy evidence. Date pits have been seized from inside the house and have been sent for DNA testing. AKM Nazmul Kader, officer-in-charge of Rangpur Kotwali police station, said preparations were under way to file a murder case over the incident.

Meanwhile, students of Rangpur Zilla School formed a human chain in front of the school this afternoon to protest the killing of the four family members. They demanded that those involved in the murders be swiftly brought to justice.

item.title: TOP SHOTS (23 August 2023)
Reimagining luxury: House of Ahmed enters a new chapter
item.description:
A new address. A new experience. And, more importantly, a new way of imagining what a Bangladeshi luxury fashion house can become.

House of Ahmed on Friday opened the doors to its new outlet at Ventura Mall, Gulshan 2, marking the beginning of Chapter 2 for the brand. Spanning approximately 4,500 square feet across two floors, the new space is more than a retail destination. It is an extension of the House of Ahmed universe, where couture, craftsmanship and hospitality come together.

For House of Ahmed, this new chapter is not simply about rebuilding. It is about reimagining, rethinking the customer experience, sharpening the brand’s design language and creating a stronger vision for the future.

Speaking about the new chapter, Ahmed Tuhin Reza, co-founder, House of Ahmed, said, "Chapter 2 is deeply personal for us. What we have experienced has tested us in ways we had not anticipated, but it has also reminded us why we started House of Ahmed in the first place. We believe Bangladesh has the talent, craftsmanship and heritage to create luxury that can stand proudly anywhere in the world. We chose to move forward because we believe in that vision. Chapter 2 is not about going back to where we were; it is about moving forward with greater clarity, stronger purpose and an even bigger ambition."

House of Ahmed is rooted in Bangladeshi heritage, craftsmanship and contemporary design. The brand seeks to bring the richness of South Asian artistry into modern couture while maintaining a distinctly Bangladeshi identity. Traditional art forms and textiles, including zardori and Bangladeshi damdaani, are part of its wider ambition to take expressions of Bangladeshi craftsmanship to the world.

The press conference was held in the afternoon, setting the stage for the main event later in the evening. Unlike a conventional launch or fashion event, however, the evening was refreshingly free of elaborate formalities. Instead, it unfolded as an intimate and celebratory gathering, bringing together House of Ahmed’s loyal customers, celebrities, models, fashion personalities and close friends of the brand.

As the evening progressed, their presence transformed the occasion into something truly special. The gathering seemed to sparkle with familiar faces, creating an atmosphere that was warm, vibrant and effortlessly glamorous. It was less about ceremony and more about celebrating the enduring relationship between House of Ahmed and the people who have supported and shaped its journey. For a few hours, the venue came alive like a constellation of stars, reflecting the brand’s growing presence and its strong connection with the fashion community.

From fashion to experience

The new outlet has been conceived as more than a place to view or purchase clothing. The space is designed to offer customers the experience of entering a luxury fashion house.

Across its two floors, customers will encounter distinct yet connected experiences. One area allows them to explore curated collections, while more intimate spaces are dedicated to couture, bridal and bespoke consultations. The journey is designed to move naturally from discovery to deeper personalisation.

The interior follows the same philosophy that defines the brand’s clothing, heritage interpreted through a contemporary lens. The space is refined, warm and sophisticated, while keeping the craftsmanship of the garments at the centre. Elements inspired by the textures and embellishment of the garments have also been incorporated into different parts of the store, creating a visual connection between the clothes and their surroundings.

From couture to everyday premium wear

The new outlet brings together House of Ahmed’s signature couture and occasion-wear, alongside bridal and festive collections. But the brand is also expanding the idea of luxury beyond special occasions.

Its Friday Signature Collection offers everyday premium wear, creating another entry point into the House of Ahmed world.

Chapter 2 also introduces new expressions of the brand’s design language, including specially curated pieces. The brand also plans to introduce exclusive and limited-edition creations, giving customers opportunities to experience something more distinctive.

A more personalised experience

Customer experience is central to this new chapter.

From the first consultation to the final fitting, House of Ahmed wants every interaction to feel personal, thoughtful and worthy of the occasion.
Its bespoke service allows customers to work directly with the team on silhouettes, fabrics, colours, embroidery, detailing and finishing, creating garments that feel uniquely theirs.

A personal touch for bridal

Bridal couture remains an important part of House of Ahmed’s identity, and the new outlet gives the brand greater scope to make that experience even more personal.

The bridal journey begins with understanding the bride, her vision for the wedding, her personal style, the ceremonies and the emotions she wants her wardrobe to express.

From there, the House of Ahmed team works through design, fabric, craftsmanship, fittings and finishing to create a complete bridal vision.
Couture and bridal clients will also have access to personalised consultations and private appointments. Styling, fabric selection, silhouette, embroidery, fitting and personalisation will all form part of an integrated experience.

For Tenzila Elma, co-founder, House of Ahmed, this new chapter represents the emotional and creative evolution of the house.
“For us, luxury has always been about more than a garment. It is about the hands that create it, the stories woven into it and the culture that gives it meaning. Chapter 2 gives us an opportunity to look at everything we have built, refine it and take it further. We want House of Ahmed to become a name that represents the beauty of Bangladesh with confidence, where our heritage is not simply preserved, but reimagined for a new generation and a global audience.”

Heritage with a contemporary voice

At the heart of House of Ahmed is a deep connection to Bangladesh’s textile traditions, artisanal skills and cultural heritage.

The brand positions itself as a Bangladeshi luxury fashion house that brings the richness of South Asian artistry into modern couture while maintaining a distinctly Bangladeshi identity.

This vision is supported by a production ecosystem involving more than 500 artisans, specialising in embroidery, hand embellishment, textile work, finishing and other traditional techniques.

Creating a highly detailed couture piece can take weeks or even months, depending on the complexity of the design and the level of hand craftsmanship involved. Every layer of embroidery, embellishment and finishing demands patience, precision and time.

What “Luxury Made in Bangladesh” means

This commitment to craftsmanship lies at the heart of House of Ahmed’s idea of “Luxury Made in Bangladesh.”

For the brand, the phrase is not simply about where a garment is produced. It is about creating world-class fashion without losing the identity of its origin, putting Bangladeshi craftsmanship, creativity and cultural heritage on the same stage as global luxury.
It is a philosophy that allows the brand to look outward without losing sight of where it comes from.

It is about refining a design language, creating a deeper relationship with customers, bringing heritage into contemporary luxury and demonstrating what Bangladeshi craftsmanship can mean on a global stage.

Introducing Ilaf

One of the key developments of Chapter 2 is Ilaf, a new proposition from House of Ahmed exploring another expression of tradition.
Rooted in craftsmanship but designed for a younger, more versatile and everyday occasion-led customer, Ilaf is aimed at people who appreciate design, quality and cultural detail but want greater versatility in their wardrobes.

It allows House of Ahmed to address a wider range of occasions and customers without diluting the identity of its main couture house.
While House of Ahmed remains rooted in couture, ceremony and occasion-led luxury, Ilaf will be more fluid, traditional yet versatile. The two will share a commitment to craftsmanship but express it through different design languages and customer experiences.

Ilaf will also be positioned at a more accessible price point than traditional House of Ahmed couture, making elevated design and craftsmanship available to a wider audience.

Bangladesh at its heart, the world as its audience

The opening of the new House of Ahmed is therefore more than the launch of another fashion outlet. It marks the next stage in the evolution of a brand with a much larger ambition.

Over the coming years, House of Ahmed aims to establish itself as a recognised South Asian luxury house with Bangladesh at its heart and the world as its audience.

Its plans include strengthening its couture offering, expanding its retail and international presence, developing new propositions such as Ilaf and continuing to invest in the craftsmanship that defines the house.
Ultimately, Chapter 2 is about more than creating new collections or opening a new space.

It is about refining a design language, creating a deeper relationship with customers, bringing heritage into contemporary luxury and demonstrating what Bangladeshi craftsmanship can mean on a global stage.

House of Ahmed is not simply opening a new chapter. It is reimagining luxury.

item.title: 10 years of Rohingya crisis: Shama urges global push for repatriation
item.description:
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam on Sunday called for concerted international efforts to ensure that the Rohingya refugees’ 10-year stay in Bangladesh does not become 20 years, stressing that their long-term solution lies in a safe and dignified return to their homeland.
She made the remarks at a seminar titled “10 Years of the Rohingya Crisis: From Humanitarian Assistance to Sustainable Solutions” at a hotel in Dhaka.
Shama Obaed said the Rohingya deserve more than survival, including a future, a home, security, and the right to return to their homeland with dignity and peace.
“Bangladesh will stand by the Rohingya. But Bangladesh should not have to stand alone. Let us work together to create an environment for the Rohingya to return home safely, voluntarily, with dignity and hope,” she said.
She said the crisis was not merely a humanitarian obligation but also a political and moral responsibility that the international community must shoulder collectively.
The state minister said Bangladesh had previously gained experience in pursuing Rohingya repatriation in 1978 and 1992 under the leadership of President Ziaur Rahman and then prime minister Khaleda Zia.
“The situation today is much more complex. Yet the principle remains unchanged,” she said, adding that Bangladesh would continue working through bilateral and multilateral channels to facilitate a dignified and sustainable return.
Shama Obaed said humanitarian assistance should not become an excuse for international inaction.
“Bangladesh can provide shelter. Bangladesh can provide humanitarian assistance. Bangladesh can help preserve dignity. But humanitarian generosity cannot become an excuse for international inaction,” she said.
She also called on international partners not to allow humanitarian fatigue to turn into humanitarian abandonment, noting that food, nutrition, education, and protection were essential to the Rohingya and host communities.
The state minister said the needs of host communities in Cox’s Bazar must also be addressed, as they have shared land, resources, and communities with the refugees while facing impacts on their livelihoods and environment.
“Support for host communities is not an optional addition to the humanitarian response. It is an essential part of it,” she said.
Shama Obaed said humanitarian assistance alone could not resolve the crisis, emphasizing that the crisis originated in Myanmar and that a sustainable solution must ultimately be found there.
“The ultimate goal is the safe, voluntary, dignified, and sustainable return of the Rohingya to Rakhine State,” she said.
She said the Rohingya themselves had repeatedly expressed their desire to return to Myanmar and that their aspirations should be respected.
“A refugee camp should never become a permanent substitute for a homeland,” she said.
The state minister also called for an accelerated verification process based on agreed bilateral documents, including consideration of children born in the camps and those who arrived from Rakhine State since 2017.
“Accurate information is essential. Credible verification is essential, and a credible verification process can become an important confidence-building measure between the 2 sides,” she said.
She said Bangladesh would continue engaging through bilateral channels, the United Nations, regional mechanisms, and international partners.
Shama Obaed said Bangladesh had responded to a humanitarian emergency 10 years ago but was now facing a prolonged political crisis.
She expressed confidence that Bangladesh would be able to facilitate the return of the Rohingya to their homeland, citing the country’s previous experience with repatriation.

item.description:
Five people died of dengue, and 839 new patients were hospitalized across the country in the 24 hours until 8am on Sunday.

Since January 1 this year, a total of 28,929 dengue patients were admitted to hospitals across the country.
Of them, 26,896 have been discharged during this period after recovery.

item.title: Junior scholarship exams to begin Dec 8
item.description:
The schedule for this year's Junior Scholarship Examination for class eight students has been published, with the nationwide examination set to begin on December 8 and end on December 15.
The Dhaka Education Board published the examination schedule on its website on Sunday, saying the examinations will generally be held from 10am to 1pm.
According to the schedule, the examination will be held in Bengali on December 8, English on December 10, Mathematics on December 13, and Science and Bangladesh and Global Studies on December 15.
According to special instructions issued for the examinees, they must take their seats in the examination halls at least 30 minutes before the start of the examinations.
The examinations will be conducted according to the time specified on the question papers, it said.
Separate one hour and 30 minutes will be allocated for Science and Bangladesh and Global Studies, meaning a total of three hours will be available for the two subjects.
The examinees have been asked to collect their admit cards from their respective heads of institutions at least seven days before the examination.
They must correctly write and fill in the designated circles on the OMR answer sheets with their roll and registration numbers, subject codes and other required information. The answer sheets must not be folded under any circumstances.
The examinees will be allowed to use board-approved ordinary scientific calculators.
No person other than the centre secretary and examinees will be allowed to bring mobile phones or any electronic devices into the examination centre.

item.title: 2 held over killings of four family members in Rangpur
item.description:
Police arrested two youths early Sunday in connection with the recovery of the bodies of a retired Rangpur Zilla School teacher, his wife and their two children from their home in Machuapara, Kamal Kachna area of Rangpur city.
The accused were identified as Siddhartha Das, 23, and Mugdha Das, 19. They were detained from Dakhiganj cremation ground in the city. Both are residents of Machuapara.
The incident occurred on Thursday night in the area, but police recovered the bodies of the four family members on Saturday night.
The deceased were identified as Ganapati Chakraborty, 65, his wife Pritilata Chakraborty, 50, their daughter Prarthi Chakraborty, 24, a master’s student, and their 12-year-old son Priyam Chakraborty, a Class V student at Rangpur Zilla School.
Meanwhile, hundreds of students of Rangpur Zilla School boycotted classes and staged demonstrations on Sunday, demanding the arrest and death penalty of those responsible for the killings.
They marched to the offices of the Rangpur Metropolitan Police Commissioner and the district administration and submitted separate memorandum demanding the immediate arrest of the suspects and justice.
Later, they held a human chain and demonstration on a main road in front of the school.
At a press conference on Sunday, Rangpur Metropolitan Police Commissioner Mohammad Abdul Mabud said the two suspects had allegedly been consuming yaba on the roof of Ganapati’s house late Thursday night when the retired teacher heard the noise and went upstairs. After seeing them, Ganapati reportedly told them to stop taking drugs. The suspects then allegedly strangled him with a gamcha, or towel.
Hearing his cries, his wife Pritilata and daughter Prarthi came to the rooftop and were also allegedly strangled. The suspects then entered the house and killed Priyam, the couple’s only son, in the same way, the commissioner said.
The suspects allegedly remained inside the house throughout Thursday night. They reportedly showered in the bathroom, ate dates from the dining table and consumed yaba.
They also allegedly soaked the mobile phones of Ganapati and Pritilata in water mixed with washing powder to remove their fingerprints, according to police.
The suspects reportedly stayed inside the house until Friday morning and left when the area became quieter during Friday prayers. They allegedly ransacked the house to make the killings appear to be part of a robbery.
Police said the suspects later hid the stolen gold ornaments in an abandoned area behind a temple near the house. The ornaments were recovered based on information provided by the suspects.
Commissioner Mabud, who became emotional while describing the killings, said the suspects had confessed to killing all four victims after their arrest.
A murder case has been filed in connection with the incident, he added.
Family members and locals said Ganapati had lived in the house with his family after retiring from Rangpur Zilla School. He later practised as a homeopathic doctor.
His sister, Puja Chakraborty, said the family had been unreachable since Thursday night. Despite repeated phone calls, she could not contact Pritilata or any other family member, while all four phones at the house were switched off.
Concerned relatives went to the house on Saturday night and found the main gate locked. After being informed, police and Fire Service personnel arrived at around 10:45pm and broke open the door.
They found one body inside a room and three others near the rooftop area.
The bodies were recovered early Sunday and sent to the Rangpur Medical College Hospital morgue for autopsies.
A Criminal Investigation Department (CID) crime scene team collected evidence and cordoned off the house.
CID Rangpur Superintendent of Police Sumit Chowdhury said investigators initially suspected the incident was linked to a robbery. As the killings had occurred about two days earlier, the bodies had already begun to decompose, he said.

item.title: 'New policy for primary education within a month'
item.description:
State Minister for Primary and Mass Education Bobby Hajjaj on Sunday said a new policy will be formulated within a month to ensure effective management, monitoring and accountability of primary education activities.
"All officials and employees in the primary education sector will discharge their duties in line with the new policy, while activities of government primary schools will also be conducted accordingly," he said.
The state minister was speaking as the chief guest at a daylong training workshop titled "Conducting Class Activities, Monitoring, Accountability and Reform of Administrative Structure in Primary Education of Bangladesh" at the Shilpakala Academy here.
"We will formulate the new policy within a month . . . The primary education family and government primary schools will also be run accordingly," Bobby Hajjaj said.
Highlighting the government's plans for the development of primary education, he said members of the primary education family were working relentlessly to build an educated Bangladesh in line with the prime minister's vision.
He said efforts were underway to ensure that the implementation of the government's electoral pledges becomes visible within a short time.
"The primary education family will be the key force in realising the prime minister's dream for Bangladesh," he said.
Deputy Director of Primary Education in Barisal Division Nilufa Yasmin presided over the workshop.
Director (Planning and Development) of the Directorate of Primary Education Mirajul Islam Ukil and Deputy Secretary (Administration-1) Mohammad Sakhawat Hossain Sarker attended the event as special guests.
Officials and employees from different levels of the primary education sector attended the workshop, where various aspects of classroom activities, monitoring, accountability and reform of the administrative structure were discussed.

item.title: Swapon calls for expanding tree plantation social movement
item.description:
The prime minister's political adviser, Zahir Uddin Swapon, on Sunday called for expanding the ongoing social movement for tree plantation and greening.
He made the call at a discussion organized by the Krishibid Association as part of a tree plantation program at the Bangladesh Agricultural Research Institute auditorium in Gazipur.
Zahir Uddin Swapon said, “It is our moral responsibility to take care of the environment and ecosystem. For sustenance in the universe, we have to depend on the ecosystem. So, instead of limiting ourselves to mechanical development, we have to work by cultivating intellect and conscience to create a habitable earth for future generations.”
Highlighting the global context of the climate crisis, he said temperatures are rising due to carbon emissions caused by excessive use of fossil fuels. Coastal low-lying areas face the risk of being inundated, he said, adding there is no alternative to greening and afforestation to overcome this global crisis.
Swapon recalled that Shaheed President Ziaur Rahman had taken far-sighted initiatives for environmental conservation and launched the tree plantation movement alongside ensuring food security in the country.
In continuation of that, the present government, under the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, has adopted a mega plan to plant 250 million trees over the next five years, he said, adding that this year’s target has already been successfully achieved.
He strongly urged for extensive expansion of greening across the country with the participation of every family, educational institution, and social organization under the concept “One Child, One Tree."
At the same time, he called upon the agriculturalist community to play a leading role in making the social movement a success.
Agriculturist Dr Kamruzzaman Kaiser presided over the program while Nurul Islam Nayan MP, Shahidul Islam Bablu MP, Secretary of the Ministry of Agriculture Selim Khan, and leaders of the Krishibid Association spoke on the occasion.

item.title: Bangladesh's Sadia Haque appointed UN advocate for South Asia on women in digital trade
item.description:
Sadia Haque, co-founder and CEO of ShareTrip, has been appointed by the UN Trade and Development (Unctad) as an eTrade for Women Advocate for South Asia for the 2026–27 term.
She is the first Bangladeshi appointed to the role.
The eTrade for Women initiative appoints a small number of women business leaders worldwide to carry the concerns of women digital entrepreneurs into policy discussions with governments and regulators.
Previous advocates have been drawn from Kenya, Egypt, Colombia, Malaysia, Senegal, Nigeria, the Philippines, and India.
In the role, Sadia Haque will represent the region's women-led digital businesses in dialogue on digital trade and the digital economy, and will contribute to the initiative's Masterclasses and community programs across South Asia.
Her designation will be formally announced at Unctad in Geneva in September.
"I'm honoured to take on this role at a time when South Asia's digital economy is creating new opportunities for women entrepreneurs. I know from experience that building a technology business takes more than a good idea, it takes access to networks, capital, knowledge and an ecosystem that gives women the opportunity to lead. I hope to use this platform to bring the experiences of women entrepreneurs in our region into the policy conversation and help make the path easier for those coming next," Sadia Haque said.
She co-founded ShareTrip with Kashef Rahman.
Under her leadership, the platform introduced automatic refunds, date changes, and cancellations, none of which existed in the Bangladeshi market at the time and built the country's largest domestic hotel and resort inventory, bringing hundreds of local properties online for the first time.
ShareTrip became the first superbrand in the travel sector and has also won at the World Travel Awards for six consecutive years, with recognition dating back to 2018.
In addition, Sadia Haque has already received several honours in recognition of her contributions, including the Philip Kotler Awards' "Women Leader of the Year" in 2023, the "ICT Woman of the Year" title at the 9th Brac Bank–The Daily Star ICT Awards in 2024, and "Outstanding Woman in Business" at the 23rd DHL–The Daily Star Bangladesh Business Awards in 2025.

item.title: Guardian Life Insurance holds annual sales conference
item.description:
Guardian Life Insurance Limited celebrated the dedication and achievements of its sales force at the Annual Sales Conference 2026, held under the spirited theme “Odommo Guardian” in Cox’s Bazar.
The conference brought together more than 900 sales leaders and financial advisors from across Bangladesh to celebrate their achievements, recognize outstanding contributions and strengthen camaraderie within Guardian’s sales community.
A key highlight of the event was the recognition of 18 outstanding performers for their exceptional contributions and achievements during the past year.
Tapan Chowdhury, co-founder and sponsor of Guardian, addressed the participants through a video message, saying: “Guardian has reached where it is today because of your relentless effort, dedication, courage and personal sacrifices. You are the real players on the field and the driving force behind every achievement we have made. Today, we have been able to extend insurance protection to more than 13.2 million people, and this is an achievement we can all take pride in. You are the true strength of Guardian, the real heroes of our success, and you are Odommo Guardian.”
Syed Nasim Manzur, sponsor director of Guardian, was present at the conference.
Addressing the gathering, he said: “The trust Guardian has earned over the years stems from the honesty, professionalism and hard work of our people. As Odommo Guardian, our shared goal is to bring every family in Bangladesh under the protection of insurance, and we can move closer to that goal by facing every challenge together with integrity, commitment and determination.”
Sheikh Rakibul Karim, CEO of Guardian Life, said: “At Guardian, our progress is driven by the people who work tirelessly every day. Their commitment, discipline and dedication have shaped our achievements and enabled us to fulfil the promises we make to our customers. This occasion gives us an opportunity to recognize their invaluable contributions and celebrate the people behind our success.”
Mahmudur Rahman Khan, chief retail business officer of Guardian, said: “Our strength in the retail business comes from the relationships our people build with customers every day. By staying close to their needs and earning their trust, we can take insurance protection to more families across the country.”
The conference also featured performance-review sessions and strategic-planning workshops, during which participants reflected on recent progress and discussed the company’s priorities for the year ahead.

item.title: NCC Bank donates ambulance to Zia Heart Foundation, Dinajpur
item.description:
As part of its CSR initiatives, NCC Bank PLC has provided a modern ambulance equipped with medical facilities to Zia Heart Foundation, Dinajpur, to support emergency healthcare services for cardiac patients in the region.
Recently at the Secretariat, in the presence of Prof Dr AZM Zahid Hossain, Minister for Women and Children Affairs and Social Welfare, and Farzana Sharmin, MP, State Minister for Social Welfare, Md Nurun Newaz Salim, chairman of NCC Bank, handed over the keys of the ambulance to AKM Azad, general secretary of Zia Heart Foundation, Dinajpur.
Dr Mohammad Abu Yusuf, secretary, Ministry of Social Welfare; Engineer Abdus Salam, vice chairman, Khairul Alam Chaklader, director and chairman of the executive committee; M Shamsul Arefin, managing director; Md Zakir Anam, additional managing director of NCC Bank; Khalekuzzaman Babu, senior member of the governing board, Anwarul Kabir, treasurer; Prof Shah Alam Ashrafi, development advisor; Syed Mezba Alam, CEO; Md Rafiqul Islam, assistant officer of Zia Heart Foundation, Dinajpur; and other officials from both organizations were present on the occasion.
Speaking at the event, Prof Dr AZM Zahid Hossain, MP, Minister for Women and Children Affairs and Social Welfare appreciated NCC Bank for undertaking the initiative.
He said the government is working to improve the country’s overall healthcare and medical services and emphasized the importance of greater participation by the private sector in strengthening the healthcare system.
He hoped that other corporate organizations would also come forward and play a more active role in CSR initiatives for the welfare of the people.
Md Nurun Newaz Salim, chairman of NCC Bank, said: “Since its inception, NCC Bank has been contributing to the socio-economic development of the country alongside its banking operations. As part of our CSR initiatives, we have been working in various areas, including education, healthcare, support for marginal farmers, financing for agricultural research, assistance to disadvantaged and underprivileged people, development of environmentally friendly ecosystems to improve the livelihoods of people living in char areas, and humanitarian assistance for persons with disabilities. We remain committed to supporting people from different segments of society. As part of these continued efforts, NCC Bank has provided a modern ambulance equipped with medical facilities to Zia Heart Foundation, Dinajpur.”

item.title: Chevron, Asian University for Women conclude Math and Science Summer School 2026
item.description:
The Asian University for Women (AUW) campus in Chittagong recently hosted a ceremony to mark the closing of the 2026 “Math and Science Summer School”.
Supported by Chevron Bangladesh, the program concluded with the awarding of certificates to 104 bright college girls from across the country who had successfully completed the intensive four-week program.
The chief guest of the ceremony was Md Ziauddin, Divisional Commissioner, Chittagong.
Joining him on the dais were distinguished guests including Ashiq Rahman, director of operations, Chevron Bangladesh, and Dee Bourbon, lead advisor community partnerships at Chevron.
Their presence underscored Chevron’s long-standing partnership with AUW and its dedication to building an inclusive education system for women in Bangladesh.
From AUW, Mohiuddin Ahsanul Kabir Chowdhury, director of the Summer School, extended his heartfelt gratitude to the students and faculty for their dedication and hard work, noting that the program continues to serve as a beacon of opportunity for young women across the country.
Ashiq Rahman, director of operations, Chevron Bangladesh, said: "Chevron is proud to support the Math and Science Summer School since 2019. Through initiatives like this, we aim to encourage more young women to pursue STEM education and unlock their potential."
Dee Bourbon, lead advisor, community partnerships, Chevron, said: "We are proud to support a program that helps young women build confidence, expand their knowledge, and pursue opportunities that can shape their futures.
Chief guest Md Ziauddin, Divisional Commissioner, Chittagong, praised AUW and Chevron Bangladesh for their continued commitment to advancing women’s education and preparing future leaders in Stem.
He emphasized that initiatives such as the Summer School play a vital role in shaping the next generation of scientists, innovators and changemakers.
A highlight of the event was the presentation of the "Emerging Woman Leader in Stem” award to nine outstanding participants in recognition of their exceptional performance and leadership potential.
Since its inception in 2019, the Chevron Bangladesh-supported AUW Summer School has given 477 young women from across Bangladesh access to specialized courses in mathematics, physics, chemistry, computer programming, and public health taught by experienced local and international faculty.

item.title: Interspeed Activation, Malaysia’s Lavis to advance Bangladesh’s sports infrastructure
item.description:
Interspeed Activation Ltd recently entered a partnership with Malaysian sports arena management company Lavis Sdn Bhd to explore the development of a modern, world-class sports arena concept in Bangladesh.
The partnership is aligned with Bangladesh’s government’s vision to strengthen sports facilities and create better infrastructure for athletes and the wider sporting community.
Under the agreement, Interspeed and Lavis will work together to develop a concept for a multi-purpose sports arena for the Bangladesh Football Federation and the Ministry of Sports.
The proposed facility is expected to support football as well as other sporting activities and events.
The signing was attended by Adnan Karim, director of Interspeed Activation Ltd, and Datuk Jack Koh of Lavis Sdn Bhd.
Speaking on the occasion, Karim said: “This agreement marks an important step toward strengthening the country’s sporting infrastructure. Together with Lavis, we look forward to developing a facility that can serve athletes, sports federations and the wider sporting community for years to come.”
The concept development will explore the requirements for a modern, multi-purpose arena that can support sports development while also providing a suitable venue for major sporting events and activities.
Operating since 1968, Interspeed Activation Ltd is one of the pioneering advertising and marketing agencies in Bangladesh.
The company works across brand activation, sports partnerships and integrated marketing programs, serving clients across telecommunications, aviation, FMCG, and other sectors.

Markle is best known for playing Rachel Zane in the legal drama "Suits," where she appeared for seven seasons from 2011 to 2018.
She has maintained a production partnership with Netflix through Archewell Productions, which she runs with Prince Harry. Their projects include “With Love, Meghan," “Heart of Invictus," and “Harry & Meghan."
